questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Which of these does NOT belong when grouped with the others about Shakespeare's world?
questions.answer: The printing press, invented in the 15th century by Johannes Gutenberg in Germany
questions.why: The Globe, Elizabeth I, and Brooke's poem are all directly tied to Shakespeare writing and staging Romeo and Juliet. The printing press is a real historical invention but has no direct connection to the play's composition or performance, making it the odd one out.
options: The Globe Theatre, where many of Shakespeare's plays were performed for London audiences
Queen Elizabeth I, who reigned over much of Shakespeare's early career
Arthur Brooke's poem, an earlier source Shakespeare adapted for his tragedy
The printing press, invented in the 15th century by Johannes Gutenberg in Germany

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Match each figure or event to its correct role in the ending of Romeo and Juliet: 1) Friar John, 2) Friar Laurence's letter, 3) The plague quarantine, 4) Romeo's belief that Juliet is dead.
questions.answer: 1-c, 2-b, 3-d, 4-a: Friar John failed to deliver the letter; the letter explained Juliet's fake death; quarantine delayed Friar John; Romeo believed Juliet was truly dead and killed himself
questions.why: Friar John, not the Nurse, was tasked with delivering Friar Laurence's letter to Romeo, but he was shut in a plague-quarantined house and never reached him. Because Romeo never learns the truth about Juliet's sleeping potion, he believes she is dead and takes his own life.
options: 1-c, 2-b, 3-d, 4-a: Friar John failed to deliver the letter; the letter explained Juliet's fake death; quarantine delayed Friar John; Romeo believed Juliet was truly dead and killed himself
1-a, 2-b, 3-d, 4-c: Friar John delivered the letter successfully; the letter explained Juliet's fake death; quarantine delayed the Nurse; Romeo believed Juliet was truly dead and killed himself
1-c, 2-a, 3-b, 4-d: Friar John failed to deliver the letter; the letter warned Romeo to flee Verona; quarantine delayed Friar Laurence himself; Romeo believed Juliet had betrayed him
1-d, 2-b, 3-c, 4-a: The Nurse failed to deliver the letter; the letter explained Juliet's fake death; quarantine delayed Friar John; Romeo believed Juliet was truly dead and killed himself

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: A student explains why some animals can reproduce without a mate using this worked argument. Which step is WRONG? Step 1: Aphids can reproduce asexually by cloning themselves. Step 2: This means all their offspring are genetically identical to the parent. Step 3: Because aphids can do this, all insects must also reproduce asexually. Step 4: In fact, most insects, like bees and butterflies, reproduce sexually.
questions.answer: Step 3: Because aphids can do this, all insects must also reproduce asexually
questions.why: Step 3 wrongly generalises from one species to an entire group. Aphids are unusual in being able to reproduce asexually, but most insects reproduce sexually, as Step 4 correctly states.
options: Step 1: Aphids can reproduce asexually by cloning themselves
Step 2: This means all their offspring are genetically identical to the parent
Step 3: Because aphids can do this, all insects must also reproduce asexually
Step 4: In fact, most insects, like bees and butterflies, reproduce sexually

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Which statement about the fall of Rome and the early medieval period that followed is FALSE?
questions.answer: Written record-keeping and learning improved immediately across Europe once Rome's central government collapsed
questions.why: Learning and record-keeping actually declined in much of Western Europe after Rome fell, since Roman administrative structures and schools broke down. The other three statements are accurate.
options: The Western Roman Empire's collapse was caused by a mix of invasions, economic decline, and political instability
The Eastern Roman Empire (Byzantine Empire) continued for centuries after the west fell
Feudalism developed partly to provide local protection and order once central Roman rule ended
Written record-keeping and learning improved immediately across Europe once Rome's central government collapsed

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Put these feudal relationships in order, from the person who grants land FIRST down to the person who works it LAST: knight, king, peasant (serf), lord/noble.
questions.why: The king granted land to lords/nobles, who granted portions to knights in exchange for military service, and peasants worked the land at the bottom of the pyramid with the least power.
options: King, lord/noble, knight, peasant (serf)
King, knight, lord/noble, peasant (serf)
Lord/noble, king, knight, peasant (serf)
King, lord/noble, peasant (serf), knight

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: In Romeo and Juliet, which line best shows the theme of love and hate fused together in a single paradox?
questions.answer: 'My only love sprung from my only hate'
questions.why: This line is an oxymoron: Juliet names love and hate as coming from the same source, capturing the play's central theme directly. The other quotes are memorable but focus on conflict, fate, or farewell, not love and hate merged in one phrase.
options: 'My only love sprung from my only hate'
'A plague on both your houses'
'These violent delights have violent ends'
'Parting is such sweet sorrow'

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Put these developments of the medieval Catholic Church's power in the correct chronological order.
questions.answer: Church becomes major landowner, Church crowns and legitimises kings, Church launches the Crusades, Church's authority is challenged by later reformers
questions.why: The Church first built wealth and land, used that influence to legitimise rulers, then projected power abroad through the Crusades, before facing challenges to its authority much later — a steady rise before any decline.
options: Church becomes major landowner, Church crowns and legitimises kings, Church launches the Crusades, Church's authority is challenged by later reformers
Church launches the Crusades, Church becomes major landowner, Church crowns and legitimises kings, Church's authority is challenged by later reformers
Church's authority is challenged by later reformers, Church becomes major landowner, Church crowns and legitimises kings, Church launches the Crusades
Church crowns and legitimises kings, Church becomes major landowner, Church launches the Crusades, Church's authority is challenged by later reformers

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The First Crusade (1096-1099) was launched with the stated goal of recapturing ______ from Muslim control.
questions.why: Jerusalem was the central holy city for Christians, Muslims, and Jews, and its capture was the First Crusade's main declared religious objective.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Match each fact to its correct detail about Shakespeare's life and work: 1) Theatre he was associated with, 2) Monarch during much of his career, 3) Source material for Romeo and Juliet, 4) Century he wrote in. a) Elizabeth I. b) The Globe Theatre. c) 16th-17th century. d) Arthur Brooke's earlier poem.
questions.why: Shakespeare worked at the Globe Theatre, during Elizabeth I's reign (later James I), adapted Romeo and Juliet from Arthur Brooke's earlier poem, and wrote across the late 16th into the early 17th century.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: What term describes a play like Romeo and Juliet that ends in death and disaster, often caused by a character's flaws or fate?
questions.why: A tragedy is a play that ends in serious, often fatal, misfortune for the main characters, typically driven by flaws, fate, or circumstance — exactly the pattern in Romeo and Juliet.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: What term describes reproduction that requires only one parent and produces genetically identical offspring?
questions.why: Asexual reproduction involves a single parent and produces clones with identical DNA, unlike sexual reproduction which combines genetic material from two parents.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: A classmate says the Crusades only matter for religious history and have nothing to do with subjects like trade, science, or geography today. Explain why this view is too narrow, using at least one specific long-term effect of the Crusades beyond religion.

encore.subject: History
encore.prompt: Put these steps in the correct order for analysing a cause-and-consequence chain in history (e.g. the fall of Rome leading to feudalism).
encore.why: Good cause-and-consequence analysis moves step by step from the triggering event through immediate effects to the eventual long-term outcome, showing the chain of causation clearly rather than jumping straight to the end result.
sequence: Identify the initial event or change
Trace how those effects led to further changes
Explain the longer-term consequence or new system that emerged

encore.subject: Maths
encore.prompt: A rectangle has a base of 8 cm and a height of 5 cm. A triangle has the same base and height. What is the area of the triangle?
encore.why: A triangle's area is half the rectangle with the same base and height: (8 × 5) ÷ 2 = 20 cm². Forgetting to halve gives 40 cm² (the rectangle's area), and adding base and height instead of multiplying gives the other wrong answers.
options: 20 cm²
40 cm²
13 cm²
26 cm²
